title: Is private PAC sample complexity polynomial in VC dimension and log-star Littlestone dimension?
formal: Is there a universal polynomial p such that every finite Boolean concept class C admits a realizable, possibly improper PAC learner using some number $m\le p(1+\mathrm{VC}(C),1+\log^*\mathrm{LD}(C))$ of independent labeled examples, with error at most 1/10 and confidence at least 9/10, while satisfying $(1,1/(100m^2))$-differential privacy? The learning guarantee must hold for every distribution on the domain and every target concept in C. Computation time is unrestricted. Take both dimensions to be at least one; constant classes can be handled separately.
context:
VC dimension characterizes nonprivate learning. Finite Littlestone dimension $\mathrm{LD}$ characterizes the existence of private learning but does not determine its optimal quantitative cost.

A sample-complexity characterization should tell us how many labelled examples are necessary from the structure of the hypothesis class, rather than from a particular learning algorithm. Two classes can have the same ordinary capacity measure while differing in how difficult it is to hide the influence of an individual training example.

The quantitative issue matters even after learnability is settled. Knowing that some finite sample size works does not distinguish a useful bound from an enormous one. The proposed relation asks whether the extra price of privacy can be controlled by ordinary statistical complexity together with a very slowly growing function of online-learning complexity.
why: The problem seeks a privacy analogue of a foundational characterization theorem in learning theory.

progress.text: The survey gives lower bound $\Omega(\mathrm{VC}+\log^*\mathrm{LD})$ and upper bound $\min\{O(\log|C|),\widetilde O(\mathrm{LD}^5)\}$. The $\mathrm{VC}=1$ case is nearly understood; the general gap remains.

status_note: Literature checked on 10 September 2026; dates and review scope are recorded below.
review_note: Concrete specialization of the quantitative target following Open Question 1: accuracy, confidence, epsilon, delta, and the meaning of polynomial overhead are fixed explicitly. The survey itself suppresses these parameters. Importance is editorial; cited proofs have not been independently audited.

definitions: A concept class is a finite set of functions from a domain X to {0,1}. VC(C) is the largest size of a subset of X on which all binary labelings occur. LD(C) is the greatest depth of a complete binary tree labeled by domain points such that every root-to-leaf edge-label sequence is realized by a concept. The function log-star counts base-two logarithms needed to reach at most one. A learner may output a hypothesis outside C. Privacy requires $\Pr[A(S)\in E]\le e\Pr[A(S\prime)\in E]+1/(100m^2)$ whenever the two m-record samples differ by replacement of one record.
answer_criterion: Prove one polynomial upper bound that works for all finite concept classes under the fixed privacy and learning parameters, or prove that no universal polynomial of these two dimensions suffices. An unspecified new characterization or a smaller bound for one class alone is not a resolution.

importance.reason: Seeks a quantitative sample-complexity characterization of private learnability in terms of two basic dimensions, with consequences across hypothesis classes.
